page.layout: One printed page (p. 157), one column of running text. Running head top left (italic "civilibus.") and top centre ("Caput IV."). Page number top right. A marginal note in the right margin beside the paragraph "Mosaica regalia". The left strip of the scan is the facing page's edge and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: consilia Evangelica servent; & opera supererogationis faciant, gloriantur. Sed Paulus charitatem perfectionis vinculum, Col.3.vers.14. vocat, qui-que alterum diligit, legem implevisse pronunciat, Rom.13.vers.8. Quæ verò charitatis per genuina sua officia, lege Dei definita, præstandæ via aut ratio esse potest, extra civilem vitæ hujus cum proximo usum & consuetudinem, sine conjugis, liberorum, & familiæ convictu, sine quibus verè vita Timonis misanthropi vivitur? Scortationes-ne igitur, fornicationes, adulteria, incestus, Sodomiæ, inter consilia Evangelica, perfectionem, & supererogationis opera accensentur? Charitatem sane omnem nusquam magis exsulare, acerbioraq; & tenaciora odia nusquam magis, quam inter Monachos & Moniales obtinere, testes sunt, quotquot Monasterium aliquod, vel à primo limine, salutarunt & ingressi sunt.
main_text.head: CAPUT V.
De forensibus Mosaicis regalibus.
main_text.p: MOsaica regalia, aut proprie talia sunt, aut criminalia. Regalia vel regia sunt, leges,Regalia quid. quæ ad magistratum & judices populi Dei pertinent. Ut de electione regis: de constituendis judicibus populi: de qualitatibus & virtutibus, quibus reges & judices præditi esse, & præ cæteris fulgere debent: de sorte, vel conditione regis, ut quod eunuchus, spurius, aut peregrinus esse non debeat: de officio regis & judicum, tam in curanda ecclesiæ Dei politia externa, quam in cognoscendis & dijudicandis causis, quæ ad ipsos de-

page.notes: The initial "M" is a large woodcut-style letter, read as "M" joined to "Osaica"; the first word is given as printed. The italic running head at the top left "civilibus." is read as printed but is uncertain as a running head. The long s is shown as s throughout, and the ligature "ss" in "implevisse" is read as "ss". The first paragraph continues from the previous page. The word "fervent" is read as "servent" from the long s. The last line ends with "de-" and continues on the next page. No catchword is visible.
